newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: WIFO sees little change in Austria 96 c/a deficit.
newsitem.headline: WIFO sees little change in Austria 96 c/a deficit.

text.p: Austrian research institute WIFO warned on Friday that the nation could not afford to ignore its big current account deficit and called for a concerted drive to boost exports.

WIFO chief economist Helmut Kramer predicted there would be no significant improvement in Austria's current account balance this year. In 1995 the current account deficit reached 47.3 billion schillings.
"Austria can live with an annual current account deficit of 20 to 40 billion schillings in the short term but in the long term it is not healthy," Kramer told an economic forum here.
In a report published last week, WIFO said it expected the current account deficit to narrow to 44.4 billion schillings this year.
Kramer said Austria's export industry compared unfavourably with other European nations and called for firms to seek direct access to foreign markets.
"Austria must export more to give the economy more room to manoeuvre," he said.
Kramer noted that declining income from the key tourism industry in recent years had exposed the weakness of the country's exports. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12257
